key_insight: MPFlow learns where to open Lightning Network channels under a fixed budget to maximize routing capacity, formulated as a budgeted max-flow optimization problem on graphs.
engineering_relevance: The method can guide liquidity placement and peer selection for operators who want better payment routing efficiency without manually tuning channel openings.
method: Uses a message-passing graph policy network to score candidate channel additions.
Optimizes actions with PPO and action masking under a fixed edge-addition budget.
Trains with a hub-exclusion curriculum so the policy learns capacity-aware placement instead of simply attaching to top hubs.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on real Lightning Network snapshots across multiple seeds and unseen graphs, where it outperformed strong heuristic baselines on the max-flow objective and was also deployed in production for 4640 channel-open decisions.
watch_item: Results depend on snapshot quality and deployment constraints, and a policy trained with hub exclusion may still need careful validation before use on rapidly changing network topologies.
paper_title: MPFlow: Learning Budgeted Max-Flow Optimization on the Lightning Network with Deep Graph Reinforcement Learning
